Williamson (+22.8), Bell (+21.4) and Coryell (+21.4) moved most; Mills (+11.4) and Hamilton (+12.8) moved least.

MO-7.t:
Eric Burlison (R) won Missouri's 7th District, taking 157,611 votes (62.2%) to 89,711 (35.4%) for Democrat Missi Hesketh, the runner-up. Independent Kevin Craig drew 6,100 votes (2.4%). Burlison's margin was 26.8 points out of 253,422 votes counted, with 99% of the expected vote in. AP called the race for him at 10:40 PM ET on election night.

Nationally, AP had called 252 seats for Democrats and 161 for Republicans as of Nov. 7, with 22 still uncalled. 218 seats make a majority.

IL-15.t:
Mary Miller (R) won Illinois's 15th District with 192,711 votes to 95,350 for Jennifer Todd (D), a margin of 33.8 points on 288,061 votes. AP called the race at 9:40 PM ET on election night, and 97.58% of the expected vote is counted.

In The Watch's wave data, which compares the 2024 presidential vote with the 2026 Senate or governor vote rather than the House race, the district's counties moved a weighted +6.4. Madison (+12.6) and Calhoun (+11.0) moved most, while Brown (-8.8) and Hancock (-8.7) went the other way.

AL-1.t:
Republican Jerry Carl won Alabama's 1st District, defeating Democrat Clyde Jones 137,025 votes to 94,940, a margin of 18.1 points out of 231,965 votes cast. Carl took about 59.1% to Jones's 40.9%. AP called the race at 11:15 PM ET on election night, with 99% of the expected vote now counted.

For context, The Watch's wave data show the district's four counties moved a weighted 17.4 points between the 2024 presidential vote and this year's statewide vote. Mobile moved the most at 20.5 points, followed by Escambia at 15.4, Baldwin at 13.8 and Covington at 11.3.

CA-10.t:
Democrat Mark DeSaulnier won California's 10th District, defeating Republican Jeff Frese by 39.4 points. With 97.08% of the expected vote counted, DeSaulnier had 210,794 votes to Frese's 91,726, out of 302,520 cast. That is about 69.7% to 30.3%. The Associated Press called the race at 11:42 PM ET on election night.

The seat is one of 254 called for Democrats nationally, against 167 for Republicans, with 14 races not yet called. A majority takes 218 seats.

CO-5.t:
Democrat Jessica Killin won Colorado's 5th District, defeating Republican Jeff Crank 155,598 votes to 141,074, a margin of 4.7 points. Two independents, Mark Elworth (5,989) and Christopher Mitchell (5,334), split the rest. AP called the race at 2:38 PM ET on election night. With 94.88% of the expected vote counted as of Nov. 7, the totals may still move.

The district's only county in The Watch's wave data, El Paso, moved 13.6 points between the 2024 presidential vote and this year's statewide race. That shift is context and is not the House vote.

FL-8.t:
Republican Mike Haridopolos won Florida's 8th District, defeating Democrat Jennifer Jenkins by 169,928 votes to 149,667, a margin of 6.3 points out of 319,595 votes cast. With 99% of the expected vote counted, AP called the race for Haridopolos at 8:02 PM ET on election night.

For context, The Watch's wave data shows the district's counties moved between the 2024 presidential vote and this year's Senate or governor vote: Brevard by 6.6 points and Orange by 14.9, a weighted shift of 11.9 across the district. Those figures describe the statewide races, not this House contest.

AL-6.t:
Republican Gary Palmer won Alabama's 6th District, taking 149,921 votes to 110,957 for Democrat Maurice Mercer, a margin of 14.9 points out of 260,878 votes cast. AP called the race at midnight on election night, and 98.31% of the expected vote has been counted.

The district's eight counties moved a weighted +20.7 on The Watch's wave measure, which compares the 2024 presidential vote with this year's Senate or governor vote rather than the House race. The shifts ranged from +16.0 in Elmore to +24.3 in Talladega, with Jefferson at +21.1 and Shelby at +21.3.

FL-11.t:
Republican Joe Strada won Florida's 11th District with 193,563 votes (52.9%) to 168,184 (46.0%) for Democrat James Pericola, a margin of 6.9 points. Independent Ralph Groves drew 3,959 votes. AP called the race at 8:05 PM ET on election night, with 99% of the expected vote now counted.

For context, The Watch's wave data show the district's counties moved a weighted 10.2 points between the 2024 presidential vote and this year's statewide vote. Orange moved 14.9 points and Lake 6.3, while Sumter moved 5.6 points the other way.

UT-1.t:
Democrat Ben McAdams won Utah's 1st District, taking 174,492 votes to 65,190 for Republican Riley Owen, a margin of 43.9 points out of 249,058 votes counted. AP called the race for McAdams at 12:26 AM ET on election night.

Two independents split the rest: Jesse West drew 5,707 votes and Elias Montgomery 3,593. The tally reflects 96.2% of the expected vote as of 3:00 PM ET on Nov. 9. Nationally, Democrats have won 252 seats to 162 for Republicans, with 21 still uncalled; 218 is a majority.

IL-1.t:
Democrat Jonathan Jackson won Illinois's 1st District, defeating Republican Christian Maxwell 165,499 votes to 65,408, a lead of 100,091 votes out of 230,907 counted. AP called the race for Jackson at 8:59 PM ET on election night. With 92.87% of the expected vote counted, the totals may still move.

The district's counties all moved strongly in the Senate and governor vote compared with the 2024 presidential vote: Cook +18.1, Will +17.7 and Kankakee +14.2, a weighted +18.0. That shift is context and does not measure the House race itself.

MS-3.t:
Michael Guest (R) won Mississippi's 3rd District, taking 144,727 votes (57.5%) to 103,823 (41.2%) for Michael Chiaradio (D), a gap of 40,904 votes. Erik Kiehle (I) drew 3,157. AP called the race at 10:21 PM ET on election night, with 97% of the expected vote now counted.

In The Watch's wave data, every county in the district moved by at least 14.7 points between the 2024 presidential vote and the 2026 statewide vote, from Hinds (+14.7) to Jones (+23.2), for a weighted +18.8. Those figures describe the statewide races, not this House contest.

WA-5.t:
Republican Michael Baumgartner won Washington's 5th District, and AP called the race for him at 8:37 PM ET on election night. As of 12:42 AM ET on Nov. 10, he had 154,299 votes (51.7%) to 142,959 (47.9%) for Democrat Carmela Conroy, a lead of 11,340 votes, or 3.8 points. Write-ins accounted for 1,077 votes.

About 89.9% of the expected vote had been counted, so the totals and margin may still move as remaining ballots are tallied. Nationally, Democrats had been called the winners in 252 seats and Republicans in 165, with 18 still uncalled.

PA-4.t:
Madeleine Dean (D) won Pennsylvania's 4th District with 231,425 votes to 113,464 for Aurora Stuski (R), a margin of 34.2 points out of 344,889 votes cast. AP called the race at 8:48 PM ET on election night, and 99% of the expected vote has been counted.

The district's two counties both moved sharply since 2024 in this year's Senate and governor voting, by The Watch's wave measure: Berks by +24.6 and Montgomery by +23.3, a weighted +23.7 for the district. That shift reflects statewide races, not the House contest. Nationally, Democrats have 252 seats called to Republicans' 161, with 22 races not yet called.

FL-5.t:
Republican John Rutherford won Florida's 5th District with 188,062 votes to 145,296 for Democrat Rachel Grage, a margin of 12.8 points out of 333,358 votes cast. AP called the race at 7:38 p.m. ET on election night, and 99% of the expected vote has been counted.

MS-2.t:
Bennie Thompson (D) won Mississippi's 2nd District with 165,262 votes to 73,254 for Ron Eller (R), a margin of 37.6 points. Independent Bennie Foster drew 5,887. AP called the race for Thompson at 9:45 PM ET on election night, and 96.32% of the expected vote was counted as of Friday morning.

On The Watch's wave data, the district's 30 counties moved a weighted +17.1 between the 2024 presidential vote and the 2026 statewide vote. That is context, not the House result. Panola moved most at +27.2, Sharkey did not move at all, and Hinds came in at +14.7.

OH-13.t:
Emilia Sykes (D) won Ohio's 13th District, defeating Carey Coleman (R) 190,593 votes to 122,078, a margin of 21.6 points. Independent Sandeep Dixit drew 5,104 votes. AP called the race at 7:48 PM ET on election night, and as of Nov. 7 at 8:29 AM ET, 98.15% of the expected vote had been counted, 317,775 ballots in all.

The district's three counties all moved toward Democrats in the 2026 statewide vote compared with the 2024 presidential vote, by a weighted 16.3 points. Portage shifted 18.2, Stark 16.6 and Summit 15.6. Those figures reflect Senate or governor results, not the House race.

FL-19.t:
Republican Jim Schwartzel won Florida's 19th District, taking 198,765 votes to 122,425 for Democrat Victor Arias, a margin of 23.5 points. Independent Seth Haskin received 3,998. With 99% of the expected vote counted, AP called the race for Schwartzel at 7:17 PM ET on election night.

On The Watch's wave data, which tracks each county's move from the 2024 presidential vote to the 2026 Senate or governor vote rather than the House result, the district's counties came in at a weighted +6.0: Collier at +4.3 and Lee at +7.0.

NJ-4.t:
Republican Christopher Smith won New Jersey's 4th District, defeating Democrat Rachel Peace by 18.0 points. With 98.13% of the expected vote counted, Smith had 156,607 votes to Peace's 108,761, a lead of 47,846 out of 265,368 cast. AP called the race at 9:23 PM ET on election night.

The district's two counties both registered large moves on The Watch's wave measure, which compares the 2024 presidential vote with this year's Senate or governor vote rather than the House race: Ocean at +27.4 and Monmouth at +17.7, for a weighted +22.3. Nationally, Democrats have 252 called seats to the Republicans' 161, with 22 not yet called.

GA-4.t:
Democrat Hank Johnson won Georgia's 4th District with 217,144 votes to 45,619 for Republican Jim Duffie, a margin of 65.3 points out of 262,763 votes cast. With 99% of the expected vote counted, AP called the race for Johnson at 7:38 PM ET on election night.

Nationally, Democrats have 252 seats called and Republicans 161, with 22 still uncalled.

CA-25.t:
Democrat Raul Ruiz holds CA-25, beating Republican Joe Males 91,947 votes to 49,463, a margin of 30.0 points on 141,410 votes counted. AP called the race for Ruiz at 1:13 AM ET on election night. With only 54.69% of the expected vote counted, the totals and margin may still move.

On The Watch's wave measure, the district's counties moved a weighted +18.2 from the 2024 presidential vote to the 2026 Senate or governor vote: Imperial +32.0, San Bernardino +18.9 and Riverside +16.7. That is statewide context, not the House result.

MN-2.t:
Democrat Matt Little won Minnesota's 2nd District, defeating Republican Eric Pratt 214,254 votes to 160,636, a margin of 14.3 points out of 375,225 votes cast. Write-ins drew 335. The AP called the race at 12:32 a.m. ET on election night, and 98.93% of the expected vote has been counted.

In the 2026 Senate and governor voting, the district's counties moved a weighted 3.9 points toward Democrats from the 2024 presidential vote. Rice County moved most (+5.8), followed by Dakota (+4.7), Scott and Washington (+3.1 each) and Le Sueur (+0.9). Nationally, Democrats have won 252 seats to Republicans' 161, with 22 not yet called.

CA-18.t:
Zoe Lofgren (D) won California's 18th District, leading Shane Lewis (R) by 128,549 votes to 47,324, a margin of 46.2 points out of 175,873 votes counted. Lofgren holds about 73.1% of the vote to Lewis's 26.9%. AP called the race for Lofgren at 11:57 PM ET on election night.

As of 12:42 AM ET on Nov. 11, about 86.8% of the expected vote had been counted, so the totals and margin may still move. Nationally, Democrats had won 254 seats and Republicans 167, with 14 not yet called. A majority is 218.

IN-1.t:
Frank Mrvan, the Democrat, won Indiana's 1st District by 26.0 points over Republican Barb Regnitz, according to the Associated Press. With 99% of the expected vote counted, Mrvan had 142,213 votes to Regnitz's 83,468, out of 225,681 cast, or roughly 63% to 37%. AP called the race for Mrvan at 10:18 PM ET on election night.

The seat adds to a Democratic total that stood at 252 called seats as of Nov. 7, against 161 for Republicans, with 22 races still uncalled. 218 seats make a majority.

NY-20.t:
Paul Tonko (D) won New York's 20th District with 181,890 votes to 103,946 for Ralph Ambrosio (R), a margin of 27.2 points out of 286,085 votes cast. Write-ins took 249. AP called the race at 10:40 PM ET on election night, and 96.35% of the expected vote had been counted by Nov. 7.

On The Watch's wave data, the district's counties posted a weighted shift of +4.7 between the 2024 presidential vote and the 2026 statewide vote. That ranged from +2.9 in Montgomery and Saratoga to +6.5 in Schenectady, with Albany at +5.9 and Rensselaer at +4.0.

CA-1.t: Mike McGuire (D) won California's 1st District, according to AP, which called the race at 11:53 PM ET on election night. With 68.67% of the expected vote counted as of 12:42 AM ET on Nov. 10, McGuire had 114,640 votes to 88,475 for James Gallagher (R), a margin of 12.9 points out of 203,115 votes cast. About a third of the expected vote remains to be counted, so the totals and margin may still move, though AP has already made its call. Nationally, AP has called 252 seats for Democrats and 165 for Republicans, with 18 still uncalled; 218 is a majority.

RI-1.t:
Democrat Gabriel Amo won Rhode Island's 1st District with 111,790 votes to 44,849 for Republican Kellie Keenan, a margin of about 41 points out of 163,060 votes cast. Independent Pedro DeSouza drew 6,193 votes and write-ins 228. AP called the race at 8:32 PM ET on election night, and 98.45% of the expected vote had been counted as of Nov. 7.

For context, the district's counties moved a weighted 24.5 points between the 2024 presidential vote and the 2026 statewide vote: Providence by 26.1, Bristol by 20.6 and Newport by 17.7.

MT-1.t:
Sam Forstag (D) won Montana's 1st District with 132,003 votes to 122,694 for Aaron Flint (R), a margin of 9,309 votes, or 3.5 points. Nick Sheedy (I) took 7,522. AP called the race at 12:02 PM ET on election night, and 97.72% of the expected vote has been counted.

In this year's Senate or governor vote, the district's counties moved a weighted 8.2 points from their 2024 presidential results. Granite (+14.7), Mineral (+13.0) and Madison (+11.5) moved most. Glacier (-7.5) was the only county to move the other way.

TX-7.t:
Lizzie Pannill Fletcher (D) won Texas's 7th District with 160,454 votes, or 70.8%, to 62,387 (27.5%) for Alexander Hale (R), a margin of 43.3 points. Independent Espoir Ngabo drew 3,652. AP called the race at 9:26 PM ET on election night, and 99% of the expected vote is counted.

For context, the district's two counties moved +27.4 (Harris) and +27.0 (Fort Bend) between the 2024 presidential vote and the 2026 Senate or governor vote, a weighted +27.3. Nationally, Democrats have 252 called seats to Republicans' 161, with 22 not yet called.

IA-3.t:
Sarah Trone Garriott (D) won Iowa's 3rd District, defeating Zach Nunn (R) by 189,351 votes to 163,635, a margin of 7.3 points out of 352,986 cast. AP called the race at 12:03 AM ET on election night, and 98.84% of the expected vote has been counted.

For context, every county in the district moved between the 2024 presidential vote and this year's Senate or governor vote, with a weighted shift of +16.5. Polk, the largest, moved +15.8. The biggest moves were in Wapello (+25.1), Appanoose (+22.9) and Wayne (+22.1), and the smallest was in Cass (+13.8).

MI-3.t:
Democrat Hillary Scholten won Michigan's 3rd District, taking 211,061 votes to 152,988 for Republican Terri DeBoer, a margin of 15.7 points. Independent Joe Jock drew 5,339. With 99% of the expected vote counted, 369,388 ballots had been tallied, and AP called the race for Scholten at 12:54 AM ET on election night.

For context, the district's counties moved a weighted +7.2 between the 2024 presidential vote and this year's statewide Senate or governor vote: Kent +8.3, Muskegon +7.1 and Ottawa +4.7. Those figures describe the top of the ticket, not the House race.

CA-17.t:
Ro Khanna (D) won California's 17th District, defeating Ritesh Tandon (R) by 44.7 percentage points. With 89.06% of the expected vote counted, Khanna had 139,688 votes to Tandon's 53,377, out of 193,065 ballots in the race. AP called the seat for Khanna at 12:33 AM ET on election night.

Because about 11% of the expected vote had yet to be reported as of Nov. 11, the totals and margin may still move. The outcome is not in doubt. Nationally, Democrats had been called the winners in 254 seats and Republicans in 167, with 14 still undecided; 218 is a majority.

PA-3.t:
Democrat Chris Rabb won Pennsylvania's 3rd District with 254,163 votes to 17,361 for independent Dennis Mahoney, according to AP's count. That is 93.6% of the 271,524 votes counted to Mahoney's 6.4%, a margin of 87.2 points. AP called the race for Rabb at 8:27 PM ET on election night, and 98.48% of the expected vote had been counted as of Nov. 7.

The district lies in Philadelphia, which moved 20.1 points between the 2024 presidential vote and this year's Senate or governor vote. That shift is context for the area, not a measure of the House race.

CO-1.t:
Melat Kiros (D) won Colorado's 1st District, taking 237,993 votes to 42,906 for Christy Peterson (R). Independents Shimon Blau, with 16,604, and Chad Humphrey, with 5,154, trailed. Kiros's margin was 64.2 points of 303,789 votes counted, with 98.65% of the expected vote in. AP called the race at 9:22 PM ET on election night.

The district's counties moved a weighted 14.4 points between the 2024 presidential vote and the 2026 Senate or governor vote: Arapahoe 16.2, Denver 14.2 and Jefferson 12.9. That shift describes the statewide contests, not this House race.

PA-6.t:
Chrissy Houlahan (D) won Pennsylvania's 6th District with 198,715 votes to 110,297 for Marty Young (R), a margin of 28.6 points out of 309,012 votes cast. With 99% of the expected vote counted, AP called the race for Houlahan at 9:17 PM ET on election night.

Both of the district's counties moved toward Democrats since 2024 in this year's statewide vote: Berks by 24.6 points and Chester by 22.0, a weighted shift of 23.0. Those figures compare the 2024 presidential vote with the 2026 Senate or governor vote, not the House race. Nationally, Democrats have won 252 seats to Republicans' 161, with 22 not yet called.

MD-1.t:
Andy Harris (R) won Maryland's 1st District, which AP called for him at 11:42 PM ET on election night. With 91.51% of the expected vote counted, Harris has 159,275 votes to 138,636 for Dan Schwartz (D), a margin of 6.9 points out of 297,911 votes cast. Because less than 95% of the vote is in, the numbers may still move.

On The Watch's wave data, which tracks Senate and governor results rather than the House vote, the district's counties moved -0.6 on a weighted basis since 2024. The swings ranged from -5.7 in Somerset to +2.1 in Wicomico.

CA-2.t:
Jared Huffman (D) won California's 2nd District, beating Robin Littau (R) by 31.2 points in AP's count. With 224,190 votes tallied, Huffman had 147,094 (65.6%) to Littau's 77,096 (34.4%). AP called the race for Huffman at 11:47 PM ET on election night.

As of 12:42 AM ET on Nov. 11, only 68.85% of the expected vote had been counted, so the totals and the margin may still move. Nationally, AP has called 254 seats for Democrats and 167 for Republicans, with 14 still undecided; 218 is a majority.

With 87.14% of the expected vote counted, Clarke had 146,503 votes to 30,378 for Joel Azumah (R), a margin of 65.1 points out of 178,465 votes cast. Write-ins accounted for 1,584. Because less than 95% of the expected vote is in, the totals may still move.
